```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r attach}
library(priogridR)
```

The conversion functions can return ordinary data frames, rasters, or a
structured `pg_result`. The workflow helpers make it easier to organize,
inspect, save, and visualize those outputs consistently.

## Reproducible project paths

`pg_paths()` constructs conventional raw, processed, and temporary data paths
without changing the working directory.

```{r paths}
project_root <- file.path(tempdir(), "priogridR-vignette-project")
paths <- pg_paths(project_root, create = TRUE)
paths
```

The returned list can be passed directly to `file.path()` when creating input
or output filenames.

## Structured conversion results

Request `return = "result"` when both the converted data and its metadata are
useful.

```{r result}
events <- data.frame(
  longitude = c(10, 10.1, 20),
  latitude = c(50, 50.1, 60)
)

config <- priogrid::pg_config(nrow = 18, ncol = 36, verbose = FALSE)

event_result <- pg_from_points(
  events,
  variable = "event_count",
  longitude = "longitude",
  latitude = "latitude",
  aggregation = "count",
  return = "result",
  config = config
)

event_result
```

The ordinary tabular representation is available through `as.data.frame()`.

```{r result-data}
event_data <- as.data.frame(event_result)
head(event_data)
```

## Write outputs

`pg_write_result()` selects the writer from the filename extension. Data frames
and tabular `pg_result` objects support CSV, RDS, and—when `arrow` is
installed—Parquet. Rasters support TIFF and VRT.

```{r write-table}
csv_file <- file.path(paths$temporary, "event-counts.csv")
pg_write_result(event_result, csv_file, overwrite = TRUE)
utils::read.csv(csv_file)
```

Use explicit overwrite permission in reproducible scripts when replacing an
earlier output is intended.

```{r raster-output, eval=FALSE}
pg_write_result(raster_result, "data/processed/variable.tif", overwrite = TRUE)
```

## Plot grid data

`pg_plot()` joins a variable to configured cell polygons and returns an
ordinary `ggplot2` object.

```{r map, fig.width=7, fig.height=3.5}
map <- pg_plot(event_data, "event_count", config = config)
map
```

Add layers or replace theme components as with any other ggplot. `pg_theme()`
can also be used independently.

```{r customize, fig.width=7, fig.height=3.5}
map +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "Example event counts") +
  pg_theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Temporary example files are removed when the R session ends. In a real
project, use a persistent project root and keep raw and processed data in
separate directories.
